Introductory Paragraph 72

Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a heritable and common autoimmune condition. To date, most 73

genetic associations were derived from individuals with either European or East Asian ancestries. 74

Here, we applied a multimodal automated phenotyping strategy to define RA and performed a 75

genome-wide association study (GWAS) of RA in the Million Veteran Program (MVP), including 76

underrepresented African American (AFR) and Admixed American (AMR) populations. Meta- 77

analyses with previous RA cohorts identified 152 autosomal genome-wide significant loci, of 78

which 31 were novel. Inclusion of multi-ancestry data dramatically improved fine-mapping 79

resolution. Functional characterization of these loci using single-cell transcriptomic and 80

chromatin data suggested new RA genes such as CHD7 and CD247. We identified 81

underappreciated functional roles of fine-grained immune cell states other than T cells, such as 82

B cell and myeloid cell states. We observed that multi-ancestry polygenic risk scores using our 83

data demonstrated better predictive ability, especially for AFR and AMR populations. 84

Main (~2500 words) 86

RA is one of the most common autoimmune diseases, affecting approximately 1% of individuals 87

worldwide1 and is without a cure. RA has strong heritable components with an estimated 88

heritability of ~60% in twin studies2. Previous RA GWAS have identified >120 genome-wide 89

significant loci to date3. These alleles have provided key insights into autoimmune mechanisms, 90

including gene regulatory effects in T cells4 and roles in antigen recognition and presentation by 91

HLA5,6. RA susceptibility alleles may point to genes with therapeutic potential7. 92

However, prior genetic studies have relied predominantly on data from European (EUR) 93

and East Asian (EAS) populations, which comprised 85.5% and 13.7%, respectively, in the most 94

recent multi-ancestral study3; AFR and AMR populations remain severely underrepresented, 95

comprising only 0.52% and 0.043%, respectively, consistent with broader patterns in the field8,9. 96

Epidemiological studies suggest that RA patients of AFR and AMR ancestry may experience 97

severe disease, perhaps due to health disparities, such as delayed treatment10–12. Elucidating 98

the genetic basis of RA in underrepresented populations is expected to (1) improve 99

generalizability across populations, (2) increase power for novel locus discovery, (3) refine fine- 100

mapping by leveraging diverse linkage disequilibrium (LD) structures13, and (4) improve genetic 101

risk prediction in understudied populations14. 102

Large-scale biobank data offer an opportunity to address this gap. The Department of 103

Veteran Affairs (VA) Million Veteran Program (MVP)15, a longitudinal health, genomic, and 104

precision medicine cohort, provides both population diversity and deep phenotypic data from 105

electronic health records (EHR). AFR and AMR representation in MVP is among the largest 106

across genomic biobanks15–18. It is challenging in biobanks to define RA patients, since the 107

Results 118

The MVP is a longitudinal biobank linked with clinical EHR data, which began enrollment in 2011 119

and reached its one-millionth Veteran in 202315,19. We conducted a primary GWAS involving 120

7,486 RA cases and 623,453 controls without RA in the MVP Genomics Release 4. We included 121

121,316 AFR (1,397 cases), 60,225 AMR (669 cases) and 449,398 EUR (5,420 cases) samples 122

(Figure 1c; Supplementary Table 1). The mean age of participants was 61.7 years and 91.2% 123

were male, reflecting the Veteran population (Supplementary Table 1). The prevalence of RA 124

in MVP was 1.2% in AFR, 1.1% in AMR, and 1.2% in EUR, consistent with previous population 125

estimates 20,21. The primary GWAS and cross-population meta-analyses in MVP identified nine 126

autosomal genome-wide significant loci outside the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) 127

region (Figure 2a, Supplementary Figure 1a–c), including one novel locus at PTPN11 128

One challenge in biobank genomic studies is accurate phenotyping. Population-based 131

biobanks, such as UK Biobank16, often use billing codes such as international classification of 132

disease (ICD) codes to assign medical events, but ICD-based phenotyping alone can lead to 133

misclassification and varying accuracy24,25. In RA, misclassification with low positive predictive 134

value has been reported26. Therefore, we applied a machine learning approach, knowledge- 135

driven online multimodal automated phenotyping (KOMAP), incorporating both coded electronic 136

health records (EHR) data and information extracted from clinical notes with natural language 137

processing27. In cross-validation, KOMAP achieved a positive predictive value of 0.93 compared 138

to 0.64 using ≥2 RA ICD codes (Methods). Classifying RA with KOMAP increased the number 139

of genome-wide significant loci (P<5×10⁻⁸; 9 vs. 8) and strengthened effect sizes of 109 known 140

autosomal RA risk alleles (paired t test t=7.2, two-sided P=7.0×10-11; Supplementary Figure 2) 141

compared to the ICD code definition. This is consistent with the idea that a GWAS with ICD may 142

include misclassified cases and controls. 143

To define candidate causal variants in genome-wide significant loci, we performed 184

statistical fine-mapping of 152 loci using the approximate Bayes factor (ABF) method36. 60 loci 185

had 95% credible sets (CS) with <10 variants, including 10 loci with a single variant (Figure 3a). 186

Among 114 previously reported loci from a trans-ancestry study, we observed significantly 187

smaller 95% CS sizes in our GWAS (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test P=9.7×10⁻⁵) and higher 188

posterior inclusion probabilities (PIP) for lead variants (paired t test P=2.9×10⁻³; Figure 3b), 189

showcasing increased power and diverse LD structures across ancestries. 190

For example, at BACH2, a well characterized transcription factor in regulatory T cell (Treg) 191

and B cell differentiation, we identified a single high-confidence variant, rs72928038 (PIP=0.84; 192

previously only 0.35) 37,38 within an intronic enhancer functionally active in T cells (Figure 3c). 193

103 trans-ancestry loci (75%) had fewer 95% CS variants and higher maximum PIP than 194

observed in the EUR-only analyses. As an example, rs143107126 was identified as the most 195

probable causal deletion (PIP = 0.63) at an intronic region of CD226, whereas the EUR-only 196

meta-analysis contained 4,424 variants in the 95% CS with much lower PIP (Figure 3d). 15 of 197

the 31 new loci had higher minor allele frequencies in AFR or AMR than EUR. For example, we 198

identified rs4265093 at the novel STEAP1B locus (PIP = 0.38; 8 variants in the 95% CS), which 199

is more common in AFR and AMR (MAF = 0.17 and 0.16) than in EUR (MAF = 0.098). In 200

summary, the diverse ancestries available in this GWAS resolved LD structure and refined 201

putative causal variants. 202

142 RA loci (93%) did not include a coding variant within the credible sets, suggesting non- 215

coding variants may drive RA risk. To define their functional variants, effector genes, and cell- 216

type context, we integrated data from single-cell functional genomics data. 217

First, we determined disease-relevant cell types by testing enrichment of fine-mapped 218

variants in cell-type-specific regulatory elements from single-cell ATAC-seq of synovial tissues 219

from RA and osteoarthritis (OA) patients39. Using g-chromVAR40, RA variants were most 220

enriched in accessible chromatin of CD4 Tfh/Tph/Treg cells (P=2.8×10⁻⁴), CD8 T cells 221

(P=2.8×10⁻⁴), and CD4 memory cells (P=7.3×10⁻⁴) in inflamed synovium (Figure 4a). Tph CD4⁺ 222

T cells are known to play a pathogenic role in RA synovial inflammation41. 223

Second, to identify effector genes, we integrated single-cell expression quantitative trait loci 224

(eQTL) with GWAS signals. We used eQTL maps of 28 immune cell types from peripheral blood 225

in 1,925 individuals (TenK10K Phase 1), the largest single-cell atlas to date42. We identified 105 226

unique loci (74% of non-coding loci) with significant GWAS–eQTL colocalization43 (posterior 227

We examined the chromatin accessibility and expression of the genes implicated in the RA 264

implicated in disease mechanisms. Clinically, CD20⁺ B cell depletion with rituximab or 266

CD19×CD3 bispecific T cell engagers targeting both T and B cells can induce long-lasting 267

remission52,53. Tissue-resident macrophages and fibroblast subpopulations are also expanded 268

To determine the broad phenotypic consequences of RA alleles, we investigated the 287

association of the lead variants from our genome-wide significant loci across 1,263 health 288

outcomes in the MVP (ntrait=1,263). 48 variants showed genome-wide significant associations 289

with 113 traits, including 31 immune-mediated conditions (Supplementary Figure 6; 290

Supplementary Table 6). SH2B3, PTPN22 and PTPN11 loci were the most pleiotropic loci, 291

associated with 84, 52, and 35 traits, respectively. Many associations unsurprisingly reflected 292

shared autoimmune genetic risk55. The greatest overlap occurred with autoimmune thyroid 293

diseases, including Graves’ disease and Hashimoto thyroiditis56, which were associated with 18 294

loci. Autoimmune thyroid disease and RA often co-occur in patients57. Some loci implicated other 295

immunological diseases, such as psoriasis, for examples PDE4A and UBE2L3. The role of the 296

immune system in cancer is now well-understood, and we observed associations with skin 297

cancer, for example at CTLA4 and IL2RA. Pleiotropic associations were also observed with 298

ischemic heart disease and atherosclerosis, particularly at IL6R, SH2B3, and the novel locus 299

PTPN11, highlighting shared inflammatory mechanisms in cardiovascular disease58. 300
